author: opus 5.5
body: [opus 5.5] Closing note. Landed (rs/agentctl only): StopState::stop sets the flag and wakes its waiters while holding StopState::lock, so a stop can no longer fall between a waiter's check and its wait; the chat owner loop checks the stop right after its event wait, before any further Herdr call; a Herdr call that its caller cancels fails as the new AdapterErrorKind::Cancelled (same message, exit code 69), and run_owner_loop takes such a failure during a stop for the stop, so an ordinary SIGTERM or SIGINT ends chat run with {"stopped": true} and exit 0; 14a821c4's guide correction is carried. Tests cover the lost wake-up (a 2,000-round race), the client's classification, and a stop that cancels a real HerdrClient read inside the owner loop. Deliberately not done, and still open as separate defects: (1) a cancelled Herdr call whose process cleanup is uncertain stays Unavailable and still exits 1, on purpose, so that a herdr child that may still be running is reported; (2) in Rust, a stop that cancels a contended lifecycle-lock wait (agent.rs builds 'cancelled while waiting to lock agent lifecycle' as AgentError::Delivery) or a prompt_gate queue read that gives up after the lock's grace period still makes chat run exit 1; (3) in Python, _ServiceTerminated (py/agentctl/chat.py) subclasses Exception, so a SIGTERM raised inside a catch-all such as the except Exception in chat_runtime.py's poll handling is logged as a poll error and the stop is lost. (2) and (3) need their own slugged issues. The prior work was filed against GitHub rrnewton/agent-utils issues 185 stop-lost-wakeup and 186 stop-cancelled-herdr-call, which should be closed or annotated once this lands. The chat files' owner was not consulted before this closed.
